narrative.intro: Kiewit Infrastructure South has $387M in federal contract obligations for FY2026 to date across 3 awards, with an average award size of $129M. Obligations are concentrated in two NAICS markets: Highway, Street, and Bridge Construction with $297M and Power and Communication Line and Related Structures Construction with $90.3M. The Department of Agriculture is the largest buying agency, obligating $261M, followed by the National Aeronautics and Space Administration with $90.3M and the Department of Defense with $36M. Historical obligations show no recorded federal obligations from FY21 through FY25 and all reported obligations are in FY26. Current-year totals are partial and represent fiscal year to date activity. The firm’s award count and average award size describe a small number of large awards rather than many small awards. This snapshot describes obligations only and does not change award-value figures presented elsewhere on contract tables.

sections.heading: How concentrated are Kiewit Infrastructure South's FY2026 obligations?
sections.body: Kiewit Infrastructure South's FY2026 obligations are highly concentrated. Highway, Street, and Bridge Construction accounts for $297M and Power and Communication Line and Related Structures Construction accounts for $90.3M. FY21 through FY25 show $0 in obligations and FY26 shows $387M, indicating all recorded obligations are in the current fiscal year to date.

sections.heading: Which federal agencies buy most from Kiewit Infrastructure South?
sections.body: The Department of Agriculture is the largest buyer, obligating $261M. The National Aeronautics and Space Administration follows with $90.3M and the Department of Defense follows with $36M. Those three agencies account for the reported FY2026 to date obligations.

faq.q: What does Kiewit Infrastructure South sell to the government?
faq.a: Kiewit Infrastructure South sells construction services to the government, primarily in Highway, Street, and Bridge Construction and in Power and Communication Line and Related Structures Construction. Those two markets account for $297M and $90.3M respectively in FY2026 to date.
